title: PHP's `and`/`or`/`xor` keyword operators are rejected; `&&`/`||` are the only logical connectives
scope:
PHP's low-precedence logical keyword operators (`and`, `or`, `xor`); the corresponding AST
variants (`BinaryOp::LowAnd`/`LowOr`/`LowXor`) and diagnostic. `&&`, `||`, and `!` are untouched.

summary.headline: Logical and/or are spelled && and ||; the keyword forms are rejected
summary.body:
PHP keeps two spellings of the same connective, `$a && $b` and `$a and $b`, with different
precedence, a well-known source of bugs in assignments. Novis keeps one. `and`, `or` and `xor`
stay reserved words, so writing one is a build error that names the fix: `&&` or `||`. `xor` has
no direct replacement, since there is no `^^` operator; its error suggests `$a != $b` when both
sides are booleans, or `($a || $b) && !($a && $b)` otherwise. That is a small loss of capability
rather than a spelling change, accepted on purpose.
